rules.text: If the visible slice boundaries in a pie chart are consistent with the printed percentage labels (e.g., 45% corresponds to a 162-degree arc, 30% to 108 degrees, 15% to 54 degrees, and 10% to 36 degrees), then the label-based and area-based readings converge on the same largest category.
rules.conditions: The chart is a pie chart with printed percentage labels, and the visible slice boundaries can be compared to the expected angular spans of those percentages.

evidence.content: The yellow slice labeled 'Nuclear (45%)' spans from the 12 o'clock position to approximately the 5 o'clock position, covering roughly 162 degrees.
The red slice labeled 'Fossil Fuels (30%)' spans from approximately the 5 o'clock position to the 9 o'clock position, covering roughly 108 degrees.
The orange slice labeled 'Renewables (15%)' spans from the 9 o'clock position to approximately the 10:30 position, covering roughly 54 degrees.
The small red-orange slice labeled 'Hydroelectric (10%)' spans from approximately the 10:30 position to the 12 o'clock position, covering roughly 36 degrees.

O.reason: The angular spans of the slices are visually consistent with the printed percentages.

evidence.content: Largest global energy consumption category

B.reason: The rule correctly checks for convergence between label-based and area-based readings.

evidence.content: Route Nuclear to priority source monitoring

implication.reason: The geometric consistency confirms Nuclear as the largest category, supporting the routing action.
